links.outcome: Mortality prediction AUC/AUPRC with vs without transfer learning on target-site data
links.effect: Domain adaptation improved discrimination across all models (LightGBM AUC p = 0.0010; XGBoost AUPRC p = 0.0419); RF reached 90.7% AUC with DA and 81.3% AUPRC with ITL.
links.quote: Results demonstrated that both Domain Adaptation (DA) and Inductive Transfer Learning (ITL) significantly enhanced model performance under realistic conditions where target-domain data are limited.

links.outcome: Mortality prediction discrimination after target-domain adaptation
links.effect: DA improved discrimination across all evaluated models. LightGBM showed the largest AUC gains (p = 0.0010), and XGBoost the largest AUPRC gains (p = 0.0419).
links.quote: DA consistently improved discrimination across all evaluated models, with LightGBM showing the most significant gains in Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) (p = 0.0010), and XGBoost yielding the largest improvements in Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC) (p = 0.0419).

links.outcome: Mortality prediction performance versus established clinical severity scores
links.effect: Domain-adapted models significantly outperformed APACHE II (p = 0.0044) and SOFA (p = 0.0077).
links.quote: Notably, the domain-adapted models significantly outperformed APACHE II (p = 0.0044) and SOFA (p = 0.0077).

links.effect: Domain adaptation and inductive transfer learning enhanced performance, with LightGBM showing significant AUC gains (p=0.0010) and XGBoost improving AUPRC (p=0.0419).
links.quote: Results demonstrated that both Domain Adaptation (DA) and Inductive Transfer Learning (ITL) significantly enhanced model performance under realistic conditions where target-domain data are limited.
